summary:
LEFT BEHIND – An Atlas of Humanity in Space

Left Behind is an interactive digital storytelling platform that explores the human footprint across the Solar System through spacecraft, mission remnants, abandoned equipment, and lost communications. We developed a web-based experience featuring a Solar System Atlas, an interactive spacecraft exploration guide, mission histories, last transmissions, spacecraft status information, visual galleries, 3D visualizations, and a historical timeline.

The project addresses the challenge “Abandoned but Not Forgotten” by transforming space mission data and historical records into engaging, accessible stories. It highlights the objects and spacecraft that remain on the Moon, Mars, and beyond, revealing their original purposes, journeys, achievements, and final states.

Our goal is to make space exploration more meaningful by connecting scientific information with human stories. By preserving the legacy of these missions, Left Behind reminds us that even when a mission ends, its contribution to humanity's exploration of the universe should never be forgotten.
details:
LEFT BEHIND – An Atlas of Humanity in Space

Left Behind is an interactive digital storytelling platform designed to document and explore the objects, spacecraft, mission remnants, and lost communications that represent humanity's presence across the Solar System. It transforms space exploration history into an engaging, educational, and visually immersive experience.

What does it do and how does it work?

The platform allows users to explore humanity's space exploration legacy through several interactive features:

Solar System Atlas: Provides a visual overview of celestial bodies and the spacecraft associated with their exploration.

Explore the Darkness: Presents spacecraft profiles and mission histories, explaining their purpose, journey, achievements, and final status.

Last Transmission: Explores the final communications and lost signals of spacecraft, bringing attention to missions that have gone silent.

Spacecraft Behaviour: Categorizes spacecraft based on their operational status, including active, inactive, retired, and crashed missions.

Image Album: Showcases visual records and historical photographs of spacecraft and mission remnants.

3D Visualizations: Offers a more immersive way to understand spacecraft and their structures.

Historical Time Machine: Allows users to explore important milestones in space exploration through time.

Benefits and intended impact

Left Behind makes space exploration history accessible to students, educators, space enthusiasts, and the general public. It encourages curiosity about planetary exploration, spacecraft engineering, scientific discoveries, and the challenges of operating in extreme environments.

Its intended impact is to preserve awareness of humanity's achievements in space, promote STEM education, and encourage a deeper appreciation of the scientific and historical value of space mission remnants.

Tools and technologies used

The project was developed as a web-based application using web development technologies, including HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, along with interactive visualization techniques and web-based 3D components. We also incorporated space mission information, historical records, and publicly available space exploration resources to develop the content.

Creativity and innovation

The creative aspect of Left Behind is its storytelling approach. Instead of presenting spacecraft as technical objects or displaying mission data as ordinary information, the platform encourages users to view them as silent witnesses to humanity's exploration of other worlds.

Each spacecraft has a story: why it was launched, what it accomplished, what happened at the end of its mission, and what remains of it today. The combination of interactive exploration, historical timelines, visual storytelling, and mission information creates a unique experience.

Factors considered during development

Our team considered scientific accuracy, historical reliability, user accessibility, visual clarity, educational value, and the distinction between abandoned equipment, intentionally discarded mission hardware, retired spacecraft, and spacecraft that have lost communication.

Ultimately, Left Behind aims to remind the world that the end of a space mission does not mean the end of its story. Every object left beyond Earth represents a chapter in humanity's journey into the universe.
